title: Lower Bounds on Spectral Gaps of Parent Hamiltonians via Tensor Networks
authors: Milán Ádám Rozmán, András Molnár, Norbert Schuch
abstract: Proving spectral gaps above the ground space is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. Yet, finding lower bounds on the gap is notoriously difficult. We revisit the martingale method, originally developed by Fannes, Nachtergaele, and Werner [Fannes '92, Nachtergaele '96] to prove the existence of spectral gaps of parent Hamiltonians of Matrix Product States (MPS), and provide improvements to the different steps of the method. Most importantly, we devise a new technique which allows to compute the key quantity in the martingale method -- the overlap of local ground spaces -- exactly and efficiently. This enables a clear improvement of the method, allowing it to outperform other existing techniques to lower bound gaps, which we demonstrate by benchmarking on several models. Remarkably, our -- numerically motivated -- approach at the same time also yields a significantly simplified proof of the fact that parent Hamiltonians of any (well-behaved) MPS are always gapped.
summary: This paper presents significant methodological improvements to calculating lower bounds on the spectral gap of parent Hamiltonians derived from Matrix Product States. By introducing an efficient method to compute local ground space overlaps, the authors provide stronger quantitative bounds that outperform existing techniques. This work is vital for theoretically characterizing the stability and gapped nature of quantum many-body systems modeled by MPS.
main_problem: The central difficulty is deriving rigorous, quantitative lower bounds on the spectral gap of parent Hamiltonians associated with Matrix Product States (MPS).
main_result: The authors improve the martingale method by devising an efficient technique to compute the overlap of local ground spaces, yielding stronger quantitative lower bounds for the spectral gap.
method: They revisit and enhance the Fannes-Nachtergaele-Werner martingale method, utilizing a new formalism that transforms the key overlap calculation into a fixed-dimension eigenvalue problem.
model_or_system: The study focuses on parent Hamiltonians ($H_N$) constructed from MPS tensors. These models are used to characterize quantum many-body systems whose ground states are efficiently represented by MPS.
key_observables: Spectral Gap ($\Delta$), Overlap of local ground spaces, Bond Dimension ($D$).
important_parameters: Bond Dimension ($D$), Interaction range ($n$), Blocking size/length ($\ell$ or $r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the MPS structure is 'well-behaved' and relies on specific properties of normal or block-normal tensors.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general difficulty, then detailing the improved martingale method for computing gap bounds, followed by applying this to specific MPS structures (like block-normal) and deriving explicit spectral gap inequalities.
why_interesting: The rigorous bounding of spectral gaps is crucial for understanding the stability and correlation decay in strongly correlated quantum materials described by tensor network representations.
